title: Distancing and attribution in reporting
objectives: Distinguish attributed statements from direct assertions.
Select reporting patterns and verbs for the intended stance.
Form passive reporting structures with appropriate time reference.

explanation.heading: Meaning and use
paragraphs: A report often distinguishes what the writer knows from what another person or source claims. Attribution names or identifies that source: “The company says that the service will resume.” The sentence reports the company’s statement; it does not by itself establish that the service will resume. A reader can then assess both the claim and its source.

Distancing structures allow a writer to report information without fully adopting it as fact. “The service is reported to have resumed” attributes the information to reports, although it does not identify the reporters. If the source is important or its credibility needs assessment, naming it is often clearer than using an anonymous passive.

explanation.heading: Form
paragraphs: Reporting verbs differ in meaning and strength. Say is relatively neutral; claim can suggest that a statement is disputed or needs verification, depending on context. Confirm suggests that something has been established by the source, so it can overstate the evidence if the source has merely alleged it. According to introduces a source: “According to the council, the bridge will reopen in May.”

Use “It is reported that the bridge has reopened” or “The bridge is reported to have reopened” for a report about an earlier event. The perfect infinitive to have reopened locates reopening before the time of reporting. “The bridge is reported to be closed” describes a state presented as current at the reporting time.

explanation.heading: Examples in context
paragraphs: Compare “The supplier says it sent the parts” with “The supplier sent the parts.” The first attributes a statement to the supplier; the second makes the delivery claim directly. In a news report, “Officials say the inspection is complete” makes the source visible. “The inspection is said to be complete” omits the source and focuses on the reported state.

In a research summary, “The authors argue that the sample is representative” accurately attributes an interpretation if that is what they argue. “The authors prove that the sample is representative” makes a stronger evaluation. A cautious writer checks the source and selects a reporting verb that reflects the evidence and purpose.

explanation.heading: Contrasts and common mistakes
paragraphs: Attribution does not guarantee truth or falsehood. Claim does not always mean that a statement is false, and said to does not identify who said it. The broader context determines whether the reporting is neutral, sceptical or cautious. Avoid adding a suggestion of doubt that the source or evidence does not justify.

Be careful with time and grammar. “She is reported to have left” reports an earlier departure; “She is reported to be leaving” reports a departure in progress or planned, depending on context. After according to, use a noun phrase for the source: “according to the report”, not “according to the report says”.

examples.sentence: The company says that the service will resume.
examples.note: The future claim is attributed to the company.

examples.sentence: According to the council, the bridge will reopen in May.
examples.note: According to names the source of the statement.

examples.sentence: It is reported that the bridge has reopened.
examples.note: The passive reports an earlier reopening without naming the reporters.

examples.sentence: The bridge is reported to have reopened.
examples.note: The perfect infinitive places reopening before the reporting point.

examples.sentence: The bridge is reported to be closed.
examples.note: The infinitive presents a state at the reporting point.

examples.sentence: The authors argue that the sample is representative.
examples.note: Argue attributes an interpretation to the authors.
The writer makes a direct claim without attributing it to a source.

examples.sentence: The supplier says it sent the parts.
examples.note: The writer reports the supplier’s statement.

common_errors.incorrect: According to the report says, the bridge is closed.
common_errors.correct: According to the report, the bridge is closed.
common_errors.reason: According to takes a noun phrase naming the source.

common_errors.incorrect: The bridge is reported to has reopened.
common_errors.correct: The bridge is reported to have reopened.
common_errors.reason: To takes the base form have in the perfect infinitive.

common_errors.incorrect: Officials says the work is complete.
common_errors.correct: Officials say the work is complete.
common_errors.reason: The plural subject officials takes say.

summary: Attribution identifies whose claim or interpretation is being reported.
Reporting verbs carry different implications and should match the evidence.
Use infinitive forms to distinguish reported current states from earlier events.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence attributes the reopening claim to the council?
exercises.explanation: Says makes the council the source of the claim.

options.text: The council says the bridge has reopened.
The bridge has reopened.
The bridge reopened yesterday.
The bridge is open.

option_feedback.a: “The council says the bridge has reopened.” fits here. Says makes the council the source of the claim.
option_feedback.b: “The bridge has reopened.” does not fit here. Says makes the council the source of the claim.
option_feedback.c: “The bridge reopened yesterday.” does not fit here. Says makes the council the source of the claim.
option_feedback.d: “The bridge is open.” does not fit here. Says makes the council the source of the claim.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase correctly introduces a named source?
exercises.explanation: According to is followed by a noun phrase naming the source.

options.text: According the report says
According to says the report
According to the report
According to reports says

option_feedback.a: “According the report says” does not fit here. According to is followed by a noun phrase naming the source.
option_feedback.b: “According to says the report” does not fit here. According to is followed by a noun phrase naming the source.
option_feedback.c: “According to the report” fits here. According to is followed by a noun phrase naming the source.
option_feedback.d: “According to reports says” does not fit here. According to is followed by a noun phrase naming the source.

exercises.prompt: Choose the report of an earlier departure.
exercises.explanation: To have left is a perfect infinitive describing an earlier departure.

options.text: She is reported to has left.
She is reported to leaving yesterday.
She is reported to left.
She is reported to have left.

option_feedback.a: “She is reported to has left.” does not fit here. To have left is a perfect infinitive describing an earlier departure.
option_feedback.b: “She is reported to leaving yesterday.” does not fit here. To have left is a perfect infinitive describing an earlier departure.
option_feedback.c: “She is reported to left.” does not fit here. To have left is a perfect infinitive describing an earlier departure.
option_feedback.d: “She is reported to have left.” fits here. To have left is a perfect infinitive describing an earlier departure.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a current state?
exercises.explanation: To be closed presents the state at the reporting time.

options.text: The building is reported to have be closed.
The building is reported to be closed.
The building is reported to has closed.
The building reported is closed to.

option_feedback.a: “The building is reported to have be closed.” does not fit here. To be closed presents the state at the reporting time.
option_feedback.b: “The building is reported to be closed.” fits here. To be closed presents the state at the reporting time.
option_feedback.c: “The building is reported to has closed.” does not fit here. To be closed presents the state at the reporting time.
option_feedback.d: “The building reported is closed to.” does not fit here. To be closed presents the state at the reporting time.
